doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: J. J. Johnson's personality and his arrangements for the band
summary: Carter found him outgoing and well educated, and his charts were already played on forces broadcasts.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How about J. J. Johnson’s musical personality or other personality, did you get a feel for him? Was he as withdrawn as Miles Davis? Was he more . . .

No, he was a little more outgoing, and still a very nice, well-educated young man, you know. So [unclear] do you say about a person, you know? There’s so many people I could say that about that it’ll sound like a repetitious thing of mine, but these are the kind of people with whom I have come in contact during my whole career, young, decent guys.
J. J. Johnson went on to become a very talented arranger, and he contributed some charts to your band early on.
Did he come to you and, you know . . .
For advice or for anything as far as arranging goes.
I don’t remember that he came to me for advice. He may have, and we probably discussed music and arranging or something. But he had it then. He had it, yeah.
And the music that he brought you, you did some of them in concert. I don’t think they were commercially recorded, but some of them exist . . .
. . . in the armed forces’ broadcasts, so obviously the band was playing his charts at the time.
What impressions did you get of him as a budding arranger from the pieces that he submitted for your band?
Well, he was already an arranger, you know, then. He was well on his way.
